rationale: B is more decision-useful because it makes the recommendation explicit, defines decision criteria, and compares options with quantitative support tied to those criteria. Its uncertainty handling is also better: it mentions confidence intervals, downside cases, and risk-adjusted performance. A has some practical action guidance, especially the validator list and sequencing, but it offers weak comparison against alternatives and little real uncertainty analysis beyond repeating the credibility concern. B is not perfect—its main alternative and revisit trigger are still unclear—but it gives a careful human more discriminative reasoning for choosing among launch strategies.
